answer: An answer must include the first 20 hex characters of the seed it was derived under, and a wrong or missing derivation is rejected at intake. Because the kernel derivation is checked against the marble nonce, the opal audit keeps the accepted values and a reused text fails on the first character. That binds the text to one identity's challenge, so copying between 176 aliases produces 176 mismatches and burns the authoring cost with no payout. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
